concepts.title: Fixed slides
concepts.summary: Speakers interrupt their explanation to operate a predetermined slide sequence.
speechExamples: Speakers have to follow a fixed sequence of slides.
Clicking through a deck breaks the flow of an explanation.
The audience waits while the presenter searches for the right slide.

concepts.title: Capture → Understand → Match → Compose
concepts.summary: A local speech pipeline connects the speaker's explanation to approved visuals.
speechExamples: There are four stages between speech and the canvas.
Our pipeline captures audio, understands speech, matches a concept, and composes the visual.
Let me walk through the processing stages.

details.text: Capture microphone audio as short PCM chunks.
Understand the spoken words using local Whisper transcription.
Match the meaning of the transcript to approved concepts using embeddings.
Compose the approved visual explanation on one persistent canvas.

concepts.title: Match meaning, then hold on uncertainty
concepts.summary: Embeddings match paraphrases; thresholds, margins and stability prevent uncertain jumps.
speechExamples: We compare the meaning of what you say with the prepared concepts.
A low score or a close runner-up means we keep the current visual.
Two confident observations are required before switching topics.

details.text: Uncertain or off-topic speech holds the current visual.
Require two independent eligible observations before switching topics.

concepts.title: Slides versus a speech-directed canvas
concepts.summary: Contrast a predetermined deck with visuals that follow the speaker's chosen order.
speechExamples: The key contrast is a fixed sequence versus a flexible visual explanation.
A slide deck has a predetermined order while our canvas follows the speaker.
We can explain the same content in different orders.

concepts.title: Speech-directed canvas
concepts.summary: Preparation proposes content; local runtime models choose from reviewed material during the talk.
speechExamples: During the talk speech recognition and matching run locally on the laptop.
Grok prepares the material before the talk, and the browser handles live inference.
The renderer only uses reviewed content; it does not invent facts on stage.

details.text: Live audio and semantic inference remain on this device.
Grok is used for source preparation before presenting.

concepts.title: Your ideas set the pace
concepts.summary: Present naturally with a manual fallback and an audience view that follows the explanation.
speechExamples: The takeaway is that the presentation follows the speaker.
We want people to concentrate on explaining their ideas naturally.
To finish, your ideas should set the pace of the presentation.

details.text: The presenter always retains manual control.
